name: Anand Mahindra
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun India (2015-2022); Wikidata (2015)
forbes_bio: Anand Mahindra is the third-generation scion of the Mahindra clan and chairs the $21 billion (revenue) Mahindra & Mahindra conglomerate.
The group's operations span 22 industries from auto to information technology to real estate.
Mahindra is best known for its tractors and its sports utility vehicles, such as the Scorpio and Bolero.The company is planning to launch the electric version of the Mahindra Thar SUV in 2026.
Anand also owns a small but valuable stake in Kotak Mahindra Bank.
He relinquished his role as executive chairman and became non-executive chairman of Mahindra & Mahindra in 2020.
forbes_facts: Anand tweets regularly and has 11.4 million followers.
Mahindra is looking to launch five new electric SUVs in India and in overseas markets by 2026.
Anand owns properties in the U.S. through his family office. This includes a hotel in New York and land in Miami.
In August 2024, he was appointed chairman of the Young India Skill University set up by the Telangana state government to certificate and diploma courses.

name: David Hoffmann
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: David Hoffmann owns 127 businesses, including everything from real estate developments to luxury transportation to executive search firm DHR International, the source of his early fortune.
Hoffmann bought the Pittsburgh Penguins for $1.75 billion in June, a price that NHL commissioner Gary Bettman described as low and a good deal.
Hoffmann is the majority shareholder of Lee Enterprises and sole shareholder of Hoffmann Media Group, which together own 154 newspapers and seven radio stations.
The self-made entrepreneur grew up in Washington, Missouri, where his dad drove a milk truck.  The family didn't have running hot water until he was in high school.
He and his wife Jerri, who moved to Naples in 2015, paid $105 million for a 24,202-square-foot estate with 12 bedrooms in the city's tony Port Royal neighborhood in 2025.
forbes_facts: Star quarterback Hoffmann got a football scholarship to Northeast Missouri State U. After an injury, he left school and later finished at U. of Central Missouri.
Hoffmann and his wife own four wineries and 1250 acres of vineyard in Missouri.
Hoffmann received the Horatio Alger Award in 2023, awarded to people who have overcome adversity to achieve professional and personal success.

name: Sam Gance
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Sam Gance started his first pharmacy in 1972 with his brother Jack Gance.
He went on to acquire a stake in the Chemist Warehouse pharmacy chain that Jack cofounded with Mario Verrocchi in 1995 with five pharmacies.
Today Chemist Warehouse has annual revenue of A$3.3 billion and over 600 outlets across Australia, China, Dubai, Ireland and New Zealand.
Chemist Warehouse dropped its plan for an IPO opting for  a merger with ASX-listed Sigma Healthcare, which was completed in February 2025.
forbes_facts: In 1976, the brothers established a successful sunglasses, perfume and suntan lotion company-Le Specs and Le Tan-which they sold in 1991.

name: Fernando De Leon
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Wikidata (2026)
forbes_bio: Fernando De Leon runs Leon Capital Group, which operates companies across various industries including dentistry, insurance and medical aesthetics.
De Leon was born in Texas but grew up in Matamoros, Mexico and commuted between the countries every day for school. He was the only one in his family who knew English.
He made his first fortune in real estate, but sold nearly all his properties before the 2008 financial crisis after noticing a preponderance of subprime borrowers among new homeowners.
As that crisis abated, he reinvested in real estate, and currently owns millions of square feet of industrial space and 5,000 apartment units across four states.
forbes_facts: De Leon represented South Texas in the National Spelling Bee in the 1990s.

name: Ajay Bhardwaj
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Hurun India (2019)
forbes_bio: Chairman and managing director of biotech company Anthem Biosciences which he cofounded in 2006 in Bangalore.
Anthem Biosciences is involved in drug discovery and development as well as contract manufacturing of specialised ingredients such as enzymes and peptides for pharma and biotech companies.
Anthem went public in Juiy 2025 and its stock was listed at a 27% premium to the issue price.
Bhardwaj has four decades of experience in the life sciences sector, including  a long stint as president at fellow billionaire Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw's Biocon.
His son Ishaan works at the company as a vice president.
forbes_facts: Bhardwaj has a B.Tech in chemical engineering from IIT Madras and a masters in chemical engineering from Louisiana State University.

name: Mitchell Goldhar
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Mitchell Goldhar founded real estate firm SmartCentres in the early 1990s, then developed more than 265 shopping centers in the ensuing two decades.
In May 2015, he sold most of SmartCentre's assets to SmartREIT (formerly Calloway REIT), for about $880 million in shares, cash and assumed debt.
Goldhar, who chairs SmartREIT, also owns various developments across Canada through his private company Penguin Investments.
This includes a stake, along with SmartREIT, in the Vaughan Metropolitan Centre, a 100-acre master planned development north of Toronto.
Goldhar owns Israeli soccer team Maccabi Tel Aviv FC, which won the Israeli club league in 2019. He plays squash, tennis and hockey.
forbes_facts: Goldhar studied political science at York University and teaches a real estate development course at the University of Toronto.
Goldhar convinced Walmart to let him open its first store in Canada in 1994, and went on to build 175 Walmart stores.

name: Ge Weidong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Hurun China (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: Ge Weidong is the chairman and CEO of Shanghai-based Chaos Investment. The firm trades stocks, commodity futures and invests in Chinese startups.
Its best-known investment is an early bet in Chinese semiconductor firm MetaX Integrated Circuits, which went public in Shanghai in December 2025, raising $593 million.
MetaX's chairman and CEO Chen Weiliang also became a billionaire following the hotly anticipated IPO.

name: Dwight Schar
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2025)
forbes_bio: Dwight Schar is the chairman of Virginia-based NVR, one of the largest homebuilders in the United States, with nearly $9 billion in annual revenue.
He founded NVHomes in 1980 and borrowed big to acquire his former employer and competitor, Ryan Homes, in 1987. The combined company was called NVR.
NVR declared bankruptcy in 1992, but reorganized and recovered the next year. Today, the company builds homes in 15 states.
Schar bought a minority stake in the NFL's Washington Redskins (now called Washington Commanders) in 2003 for $200 million.
He sold it in 2021 for approximately $320 million amid a court battle with majority owner Daniel Snyder.
forbes_facts: Schar has sold over $1 billion of NVR stock since 2003.
A former junior high school teacher, Schar has donated millions to his alma mater, Ashland University, and to his children's colleges.

name: Rita Tong Liu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026); Hurun Self-Made Women (2021-2025)
forbes_bio: Rita Tong Liu's Gale Well Group owns prime office buildings and hotels in Hong Kong.
She entered the real estate business in 1976, wading into luxury homes and later parking spaces.
She was married to a high school sweetheart, the eighth of nine sons of Liu Po Shan, founder of Chong Hing Bank.
After her husband died in 2003, she transitioned into grade A offices, capitalizing on the then-soaring prices in Hong Kong's financial district.
forbes_facts: Her grandmother worked in the family business selling groceries and brewing rice wine in Macau. Then her widowed mother built houses with imported timber.
Liu is assisted by her two younger brothers, Jacinto and Luis Tong. Jacinto is the CEO and is in charge of investments, while Luis oversees the firm's logistics.

name: Solomon Lew
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Solomon Lew chairs Melbourne-based Premier Investments, an apparel retailer.
The company is the largest shareholder in Australian department store Myer and home appliance maker Breville.
Premier's brands also include the Smiggle stationery store franchise aimed at children, and sleepwear label Peter Alexander.
In 2025, Myer bought Premier's five apparel brands in exchange for new shares issued to Premier. This will create one of the largest retail and apparel companies across Australia and New Zealand.
Following five apparel brands acquisition, Lew will join the board of Myer in April 2026.
forbes_facts: Lew says he always had an entrepreneurial mindset, working in retail after school and during holidays before opening his first apparel business on his 18th birthday.
He was the first Australian to enter the World Retail Hall of Fame, in 2016, when he was inducted along with Jo Malone and Tommy Hilfiger.

name: Abdullah Al Othaim
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Abdullah Saleh Al Othaim chairs the board of Saudi-listed supermarket chain Abdullah Al-Othaim Markets.
The chain has more than 400 stores in Saudi Arabia and some 50 stores in Egypt; 2024 revenue grew to nearly $2.9 billion.
He also chairs Al Othaim Holding Company, a private company that owns and runs shopping malls and restaurants in Saudi Arabia.
Abdullah's father, Sheik Saleh Al Othaim (d. 1979), founded Saleh Al Othaim Trading Establishment in 1956, predecessor of Al-Othaim Markets.
Abdullah Al-Othaim Markets went public in 2008; Abdullah owns a 36% stake.

name: Christian Oetker
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2014-2021); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Christian Oetker owns 12.5% of Dr. August Oetker, a $9 billion (sales) conglomerate with interests in food, beverages, chemicals and hotels.
The business began in 1891 when his great-grandfather, pharmacist August Oetker, started selling non-perishable baking powder.
After World War II, Christian's father, former Nazi SS officer Rudolf August Oetker, developed additional food products and successfully diversified.
Christian is retired. He was responsible for the food division's market research.
forbes_facts: When Rudolf August passed away in 2007, at age 90, the company's ownership was divided between his eight children from three marriages.
